inherited_methods.method: Erdos harmonic double counting over pairs (p,a)
inherited_methods.loss_step: Replace the exact multiplicity of m=pa by the uniform cap r and then sum r/m over every m<=N^2.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Which prime predecessor m/p is selected, the common-gcd scale of simultaneous predecessors, and the strong overlap among constraints for different m.
inherited_methods.consequence: It yields only S(A) sum_{p<=N}1/p <= r H_{N^2}, hence S(A)=O(r log N/log log N), and cannot see the prime-block lower-bound exponent.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Optimise each prime block separately and retain only the number of selected primes per block.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Cross-block exponent patterns, repeated prime powers, and correlations that an upper bound must forbid rather than construct.
inherited_methods.consequence: The construction gives a rigorous lower bound but its local elementary-symmetric expression is not automatically a universal upper bound.

inherited_methods.loss_step: Discard prime exponents, common scaling factors, and primes outside a fixed support.
inherited_methods.lost_information: Whether an extremal pattern survives arbitrary gcd scaling and exponent-vector links in the full integer lattice.
inherited_methods.consequence: A finite-cube optimum is a falsifier or conjecture generator only; it has no completeness reduction to all A subseteq [N].

inherited_methods.method: Unweighted hypergraph independence or matching bounds
inherited_methods.loss_step: Replace vertex weight 1/a by cardinality and forget multiplicative scale.
inherited_methods.lost_information: The logarithmic accumulation across scales that is exactly the public objective.
inherited_methods.consequence: Strong finite independence-number estimates need not improve the harmonic upper bound.

required_new_information: A weighted local-to-global certificate that keeps the identities of prime predecessors rather than only their multiplicity.
Stability under multiplication by a common gcd and under arbitrary prime exponents.
A quantitative comparison with the prime-block lower construction, not merely another O(log N/log log N) estimate.
An executable falsifier for any proposed local fibre inequality before an all-N proof attempt.
